title: Decision Heuristic Orchestrator for Safety Throttles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a decision heuristic orchestrator (DHO) that synthesizes multiple SLO signals (p99 latency, error rate, per-token cost, throughput) and emits safety throttle actions for deploy flows (canary, A/B, shadow). The DHO should provide tunable, cohort-aware thresholds, statistically principled confidence intervals, and hysteresis to avoid noisy flips. It will be the primary engine used by the rollout controller to: scale down traffic to new model variants, trigger staged rollbacks, or route to fallback model variants based on combined score and policy rules. Key constraints: preserve sub-100ms median latency for host-tier customers, ensure false-positive aborts < 0.5% for steady-state traffic, and provide auditability for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: DHO accepts fanned input: latency quantiles, error rate, token cost per request, throughput and cohort metadata
Produces a single safety action with reason codes and confidence score in < 250ms median decision latency
Supports per-cohort threshold profiles and global fallback weights configurable via Console
Includes statistical smoothing (EWMA + Bayesian posterior) and configurable hysteresis windows
End-to-end integration test with canary flow: new model at 5% traffic should be auto-throttled to 1% when combined score exceeds policy
Telemetries emitted to Console: decision_reason, contributing_signals, confidence, pre/post metrics for 30m window
Docs: design doc, runbook for investigation, and a short tutorial for PM/SEs on tuning thresholds
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Chen: Created ticket to centralize multi-signal decisioning for deploy safety. Initial scope based on recent noisy canary incidents (incidents linked below).

2025-02-18 Luca Moretti: Spike complete — implemented prototype that computes weighted z-scores across signals and exposes a DecisionScore. Observed too many noise-induced flips on low-volume cohorts; need per-cohort smoothing.

2025-02-25 Design review notes (Samira Patel): prefer explicit reason codes for compliance (LATENCY_SPIKE, ERR_RATE_SPIKE, COST_REGRESSION, THROUGHPUT_DROP). Also want rollout UI hooks for manual override and audit trail.

2025-02-28 Engineering sync: agreed on hybrid approach: combine posterior delta testing for error-rate with EWMA for latency and cost. Luca to add configurable minimum sample sizes and dynamic confidence multiplier based on cohort volume.

2025-03-03 QA run: integration test with synthetic traffic shows correct action emitted but confidence underestimated for very-high-cost anomalies. Hypothesis: token-cost variance larger than expected — will add robust scaling and transform (log cost) before z-scoring.

2025-03-04 PM feedback (Riley Gomez): Add a cost-weighted safety profile for cost-sensitive customers (ability to prioritize cost SLO higher than latency). Riley asked for a lightweight UI to toggle cost-sensitivity per deployment.
2025-03-04 Next steps: finalize decision schema, add audit logging to the Private control plane API, and open initial RFC for config UI options.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike): prototype DecisionScore service that ingests signals from metrics pipeline and returns action candidates
Phase 2 (Core): implement cohort-aware smoothing, sample-size gating, and per-profile weighting; design decision payload schema
Phase 3 (Integration): wire DHO to rollout controller for canary/shadow/A-B flows and emit telemetries to Console
Phase 4 (Tuning + UX): expose profiles in Console, add manual override, and produce runbook + rollback test harness
Phase 5 (GA): run 4 week dogfood across host customers and Dedicated, incorporate feedback, and ship runtime-1.19
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoff: aggressive sensitivity reduces customer cost/regressions faster but may cause unnecessary aborts — mitigated via per-cohort min-sample and hysteresis windows
Risk: noisy token-cost signal in short windows can dominate decisions; plan to use log-transform and robust statistics
Operational cost: decision engine adds additional telemetry and compute; constrained to <5% CPU on controller nodes and decision latency budget of 250ms
Compliance: decisions must be auditable and explainable; we will include reason codes and raw signal snapshots in audit logs
